title: chenopodium ambrosioides f. suffruticosum
intro: Chenopodium ambrosioides f. suffruticosum, commonly known as Mexican tea or Epazote, is a subspecies of the Chenopodium ambrosioides plant, a type of flowering plant in the amaranth family. Mexican tea has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, including relief from digestive issues and as an emmenagogue to stimulate menstrual flow, due to its health benefits. Its therapeutic actions include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antispasmodic properties, which contribute to its effectiveness in treating various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of Mexican tea include alkaloids, flavonoids, and essential oils, such as limonene and beta-pinene, which are responsible for its medicinal and therapeutic effects.
